reference.source: Williams Hematology / WHO classification of haematolymphoid tumours
clinicalPearls: A lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma involving the bone marrow together with a monoclonal IgM paraprotein in the serum
The circulating IgM can produce hyperviscosity, causing headache, visual disturbance, mucosal bleeding and neurological symptoms
Fundoscopy may show dilated, tortuous retinal veins with haemorrhages in symptomatic hyperviscosity
Anaemia, fatigue, lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly are common, and constitutional symptoms may occur
The somatic MYD88 L265P mutation is present in the large majority of cases and strongly supports the diagnosis
IgM-related complications include peripheral neuropathy, cryoglobulinaemia and cold agglutinin activity
Asymptomatic disease is often monitored, while symptomatic disease is treated with regimens that may include BTK inhibition or rituximab-based therapy
reference.pathophysiology: Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia is a clonal B-cell disorder in which lymphoplasmacytic cells, spanning small lymphocytes to plasma cells, infiltrate the bone marrow and sometimes lymphoid organs and secrete a monoclonal immunoglobulin M. The recurrent MYD88 L265P mutation activates downstream NF-kappaB signalling through the Bruton tyrosine kinase pathway, promoting tumour survival, and CXCR4 mutations modify disease behaviour and treatment response. The large pentameric IgM molecule raises serum viscosity and can behave as a cryoglobulin, cold agglutinin or autoantibody, so many clinical features stem from the physical and immunological properties of the paraprotein rather than tumour bulk alone.
additionalDifferentials: IgM monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
Marginal zone lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation
Other low-grade B-cell lymphomas with paraprotein
AL amyloidosis with an IgM clone
additionalInvestigations: Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation to characterise the IgM paraprotein
Serum viscosity measurement when hyperviscosity is suspected
Bone marrow aspirate and trephine with immunophenotyping
Molecular testing for MYD88 L265P (and CXCR4) mutations
Fundoscopy to assess for hyperviscosity retinopathy
Assessment for cryoglobulins, cold agglutinins and neuropathy-associated antibodies
redFlags: Symptomatic hyperviscosity with neurological or visual compromise requiring urgent plasmapheresis
Severe anaemia or cytopenias from marrow infiltration
Transformation to a high-grade lymphoma with rapid clinical deterioration
reference.prognosis: Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia is generally an indolent, treatable but incurable disorder with prolonged survival for many patients; outcome is influenced by age, cytopenias, paraprotein level and molecular features, and hyperviscosity is usually reversible with plasmapheresis.
pitfalls: Attributing symptoms to anaemia alone and missing hyperviscosity that needs urgent plasmapheresis
Spurious laboratory results, including pseudohyponatraemia and interference, from a high IgM level
Failing to distinguish it from IgM myeloma or marginal zone lymphoma
Overlooking MYD88 testing that clarifies the diagnosis and predicts therapy response
